==Problem==
Define <imath>x\diamond y</imath> to be <imath>|x-y|</imath> for all real numbers <imath>x</imath> and <imath>y.</imath> What is the value of <cmath>(1\diamond(2\diamond3))-((1\diamond2)\diamond3)?</cmath>

<imath> \textbf{(A)}\ {-}2 \qquad
\textbf{(B)}\ {-}1 \qquad
\textbf{(C)}\ 0 \qquad
\textbf{(D)}\ 1 \qquad
\textbf{(E)}\ 2</imath>

== Solution 1 == 
We have \begin{align}
(1\diamond(2\diamond3))-((1\diamond2)\diamond3) &= |1-|2-3|| - ||1-2|-3| \\
&= |1-1| - |1-3| \\
&= 0-2 \\
&= \boxed{\textbf{(A)}\ {-}2}.
\end{align}
~MRENTHUSIASM

== Solution 2 ==
Observe that the <imath>\diamond</imath> function is simply the positive difference between two numbers. Thus, we evaluate: the difference between <imath>2</imath> and <imath>3</imath> is <imath>1;</imath> the difference between <imath>1</imath> and <imath>1</imath> is <imath>0;</imath> the difference between <imath>1</imath> and <imath>2</imath> is <imath>1;</imath> the difference between <imath>1</imath> and <imath>3</imath> is <imath>2;</imath> and finally, <imath>0-2=\boxed{\textbf{(A)}\ {-}2}.</imath> 

~Technodoggo
